text:
Sean Gallagher: Dropping the latest draft of “Support + Eng SLAs by tier” here for SRE sanity check. Main things I need eyes on:
1) internal SLO targets (ack + mitigation) vs what Support/CS wants to commit externally
2) update frequency expectations (customer + internal)
3) incident declaration criteria vs “support escalation”

Confluence draft (WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/escalation-playbook-v2/sla-by-tier

Please comment inline if you can, but also ok to reply here with redlines.

Rafael Mendes: Read through. Overall direction good, but the table is mixing “Support first response” with “Eng ack” in a way that’ll get us paged for stuff that shouldn’t page.

Specifically: for Dedicated/Private it says “Engineering engaged within 15m” on Sev1. If we interpret “engaged” == page, we’ll take constant pages for single-customer perf weirdness.

Proposal:
- Separate columns: “Support first response” (customer thread) vs “Engineering ack” (internal) vs “Oncall page” (only when incident criteria met).
- Define “engagement” as “assigned owner + initial assessment started” not “pager fired”.

Tomáš Novák: +1. Also update frequency: the draft has 30m updates for Sev1. That’s fine *if* it’s an incident. For non-incident escalations, 30m updates is unrealistic + causes noisy comms.

What we’ve been doing successfully:
- Incident: update every 30m (Sev0/Sev1) until mitigated; after mitigation, hourly until stable.
- Non-incident escalation: update every 2 business hours (or “next update by <time>”).

Dev Patel: Agree we should split “Engineering ack” vs “Pager/incident”. The intent from Support side was “we can tell the customer someone technical is looking” not “wake oncall every time.”

If we can get crisp language for Support to use (“we’ve engaged engineering”) while still respecting paging thresholds, that’s ideal.

Allison Grant: From an observability standpoint, we should tie “incident declaration” to measurable triggers wherever possible, or Support will keep asking for incident status “just in case”.

E.g.:
- Hosted: sustained 5xx > X% for Y mins in a region or multi-region
- Streaming: disconnect rate > threshold + correlated with edge/service metrics (not just a single customer)
- Dedicated: scheduler saturation + queue depth / p95 latency crossing SLO for N mins

Chris Osei: +1 to measurable triggers. For reporting, it’d also help if we have a field/label that says: “Escalation type = Incident / Non-incident / Security escalation” so we can track MTTA/MTTM separately.

Rafael Mendes: On internal SLO targets: suggest we standardize on what oncall can realistically meet.

For pages (incident):
- Ack: 5 minutes (24/7)
- Initial update in #incidents: 15 minutes
- First mitigation target: Sev0 60 min, Sev1 4 hours (obv best effort, but as SLO target)

For non-paged escalations (assigned to runtime/sre during biz hours):
- Ack: 1 business hour
- First meaningful update: 2 business hours

Tomáš Novák: Re: “mitigation target” — careful not to promise root cause / full fix. “Mitigation” should be “stop the bleeding” (rollback, failover, capacity add, config change). Draft currently uses “resolution” in a couple places.

Dev Patel: Noted. We’ll change “resolution” to “mitigation” where we mean “customer impact reduced” and keep “RCA timeline” separate.

Sean Gallagher: This is helpful. Quick question: for Sev1 Dedicated single-tenant issues (one customer but large $$$), when do we declare incident vs treat as escalation?

Rafael Mendes: I’d define it as incident if it meets *any* of:
- impact is blocking production for that customer AND there is an oncall-relevant system component involved (capacity/infra/runtime) AND it requires coordinated real-time work
- the mitigation requires changes that risk broader blast radius (e.g. moving capacity, changing routing policy)

But still: “single customer” isn’t automatic incident.

Tomáš Novák: +1. Also add explicit “don’t page SRE” examples:
- 429s due to customer-side retry storm / quota config (unless many orgs affected)
- timeouts limited to a single model version that has known workaround (pin/rollback) and can be handled by Support + runtime during biz hours

Allison Grant: For streaming disconnects specifically, we should say: if disconnect rate elevated across region/model (dashboard link) => incident. If it’s a handful of request IDs from one customer, start as escalation + collect metadata.

Dev Patel: Works for Support. If we put those examples in the SLA page (or link to the severity matrix), it will reduce the “should we incident?” debate.

Sean Gallagher: Another gap: after-hours expectations by tier. Draft says Dedicated/Private “24/7 updates” for Sev1. We can do 24/7 *for incidents*, but we don’t have staffing for ongoing non-incident escalations overnight.

Rafael Mendes: Exactly. Suggest language:
- Sev0: 24/7 coverage and updates (incident)
- Sev1: 24/7 if incident criteria met; otherwise best-effort until end of local business day + handoff note; resume next business day
- Sev2+: business hours

Tomáš Novák: And add “handoff required” to the process: if we stop active investigation overnight, we post:
- current status
- what’s been tried
- what customer can do (safe workaround)
- next update time

Dev Patel: I’ll incorporate. For the external-facing copy, we’ll avoid “24/7” except where contractually required and reviewed (Rachel/Legal).

Chris Osei: Can we also align on a single set of definitions for MTTA/MTTM in the metrics sheet? If “ack” is first human response vs “assigned owner”, numbers get messy.

Sean Gallagher: Yes. For the playbook, I’ll define:
- “Ack” = first response from the owning team in the escalation channel/ticket (not automated bot)
- “Engaged” = named engineer assigned + started investigation
- “Mitigated” = customer impact materially reduced (rollback/failover/capacity/config)

Will sync with your metrics definitions.

Allison Grant: One more nit: SLA table should mention where updates live. Support sometimes updates in customer email while incident updates are in #incidents.

Recommend: “Source of truth = #incidents + status page (if public). Support mirrors to customer thread.” (and link to comms alignment doc)

Sean Gallagher: Great call. I’ll link the comms alignment page and add “Support mirrors; do not paraphrase speculative causes.”

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: If you make those edits (split columns + incident triggers + after-hours), SRE is good with it.

Sean Gallagher: Ack. I’ll push updates today and tag you all in Confluence for final pass.

Dev Patel: Thanks all. This unblocks Support training content too.
